componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Students balance atoms in the printed reaction to visualize conservation of matter

componentPlan.focusQuote: All photosynthetic organisms use solar energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar (food) and oxygen.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Students contrast energy sources reactants and products to distinguish both food making paths

overview.headline: Deep sea microbes make food from chemicals not sunlight

keyPoints.point: Photosynthesis and chemosynthesis together fuel life across Earth ecosystems
keyPoints.quote: Together, photosynthesis and chemosynthesis fuel all life on Earth.

keyPoints.point: Plants use sunlight to make food within a Sun centered food web
keyPoints.quote: The majority of life on Earth is based on a food web which revolves around the Sun, as plants use sunlight to make food via photosynthesis.

keyPoints.point: Matter cannot be created or destroyed under conservation of matter
keyPoints.quote: Remind students that the law of conservation of matter states that matter cannot be created or destroyed.

keyPoints.point: Microbes form the base of vent food webs by creating sugars from chemical energy
keyPoints.quote: form the base of food webs at hydrothermal vents and cold seeps by creating sugars (food) using energy released from chemical reactions.

keyTerms.gloss: process where plants convert carbon dioxide and water into sugars using sunlight
keyTerms.quote: Photosynthesis: The process used by plants to convert carbon dioxide and water into oxygen and sugars (food), using energy from the sun.

keyTerms.gloss: process where microbes create sugars using energy from chemical reactions
keyTerms.quote: Chemosynthesis: The process by which microbes create sugars (food) using energy released from chemical reactions.

keyTerms.gloss: organism that makes its own food from raw materials and energy
keyTerms.quote: Autotroph: Organisms that are able to make their own food from raw materials and energy, also known as producers.

keyTerms.gloss: starting substance that changes during a chemical reaction
keyTerms.quote: Reactants: A substance that changes in a chemical reaction.

keyTerms.gloss: new substance formed as result of a chemical reaction
keyTerms.quote: Products: Refers to the new substance(s) formed as a result of the chemical reaction and are written on the right side of a chemical equation.

analysis.pageCoverage: Guide comparing deep sea chemosynthesis and sunlight photosynthesis with balanced equations and food web context
